reported_mineral_classes.evidence: CRISM maps identify an olivine-rich smooth volcanic unit along the western caldera ring-fault area; the published spatial extent has not been intersected with the selected site footprint.
CRISM olivine/low-calcium-pyroxene/high-calcium-pyroxene parameter maps show pyroxene-bearing basaltic units and dunes in Nili Patera; exact area at this chosen location not established.
CRISM near-infrared signatures identify a feldspathic rock unit in the caldera; its exact lithology is debated and the reported 104-145 km2 caldera-wide extent is NOT a fraction of this site.

CRISM identified localized hydrated silica deposits on the flanks of a volcanic cone. A published approximate locality at 8.92 N, 67.29 E is about 5.4 km from this reference center and just outside the nominal 10 km square footprint.

published_observations.interpretation: Hydrated silica reported in Nili Patera by CRISM; approximate compiled location lies just east of nominal 10 km square (5 km half-width). Does not establish an absence of silica in the footprint.

methods.area: No georeferenced mineral-class polygons were clipped to the actual 5 km site. mapped_fraction=0 denotes no mapped area coverage, not absence of minerals.
methods.literature_extraction: Mineral classes summarized from published orbital spectral studies for the Nili Patera caldera, with interpretations and citations; they are not site-specific abundance detections.
methods.location_test: The approximate 8.92 N, 67.29 E silica locality was compared to the 5 km and 10 km projected square analysis footprints using spherical Mars R=3396190 m; approximate location precision limits boundary interpretations.
methods.caveat: Do not interpret published caldera-wide mineral occurrences as identified inside this 5 km footprint or as concentrations, percentages by mass, or polygon area fractions.
methods.stage2_scoring: Context only. Do not calculate Earth–Mars mineral-similarity scores from this literature profile.
